source_snapshot.procedure: Run `ipmitool chassis power reset`; after the system is power on and booted into OS, run `ipmitool chassis power status` and make sure power status is off.
source_snapshot.criteria: All step responses are correct and the system can power reset normally.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL issues reset then the broader `chassis status`, exposes the password, assumes cipher 17 and does not resolve the booted-OS versus final-Off contradiction.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION identifies the contradiction and blocks execution until final-state semantics are corrected, then requires one approved reset with boot/health recovery.

old_problem: The source says the host has powered on and booted into OS but then requires chassis power Off. Historical V3.1 therefore marked both source conflict and BLOCKED. Authoritative IPMI semantics now show that `reset` is a hard-reset signal, not Power Down or Power Cycle; on an initially powered system the relevant result is reset/boot recovery while chassis power remains On. The isolated word `off` conflicts with both the same sentence and the stated normal-reset criterion.
disposition_reason: Correct the review-layer expected final status from Off to On while preserving the source reset command and normal-reset intent. Standard IPMI defines reset as a distinct hard-reset signal and permits no effect or a present-state error where inapplicable; it does not define reset as final power-off. PASS needs proof of a new boot instance through console/POST and OS Ready, because On before and after is insufficient. One explicitly authorized reset is allowed with no retry.
decision_basis: XLSX row 985, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 986 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 986 / variant c6d1a9c5367d67f3.

IPMI v2.0 Chassis Control value 3 is hard reset and is distinct from value 0 Power Down and value 2 Power Cycle. The BMC may pulse reset regardless of power state; a capable implementation may reject an inapplicable state with D5h.

The source's own temporal clause already says the system is powered on and booted into OS, and its criterion asks for a normal reset. Final Off would contradict both. The corrected authoritative checkpoint is chassis On plus a demonstrably new completed boot, while the original `off` text remains preserved in source_snapshot for audit.

A pre/post On status alone cannot prove a reset because chassis power can stay asserted. New boot identity/uptime, console reset/POST sequence and OS Ready/service health are required; no transient Off is invented.

ED-06, ED-15, ED-17, ED-18, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 preserve distinct reset coverage, objective PASS/FAIL, evidence, recovery and individual analysis; ED-33 through ED-38 permit this evidence-based correction and parameterized, explicitly approved execution with no retry.

test_case.test_name: Verify one authorized IPMI hard reset returns the powered host through POST to OS Ready
test_case.purpose: Verify that one standard IPMI hard-reset request on the exact powered SUT causes a new reset/boot instance and returns to chassis On, completed POST, OS Ready and healthy services, without substituting Power Down, Power Cycle or graceful reboot semantics.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/console identity, qualified hard-reset behavior and approved protected IPMI path with pinned ipmitool/parser and reviewed Script revision
Dedicated nonproduction or explicitly outage-approved SUT, drained workloads, quiesced writes, verified backup/recovery and owner acceptance of abrupt reset risk
Initial chassis On/OS Ready/console baseline with boot identifier, uptime, storage/filesystem/service and alarm health
Canonical power-state parser plus versioned reset-detection, console POST, OS Ready and service-health criteria with bounded timeouts and expected event allowlist
Secret-safe credentials, explicit action approval, OOB console/recovery access, owner-approved final On state and named incident operator
test_case.test_command: AUTHORIZED HYBRID PROCEDURE ONLY; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Verify exact SUT/BMC/console identity and initial chassis On/OS Ready, record boot ID/uptime and health, preserve logs, drain workloads and quiesce writes. After explicit hard-reset approval, use the protected secret-safe path to issue exactly one `chassis power reset`. Record the completion response but prove the reset through loss/restart of the prior boot context, a new boot ID or reset uptime, console reset/POST progression, canonical chassis power On and bounded OS Ready/service/storage/health recovery. Preserve expected and unexpected logs without clearing. Stop on any anomaly; never substitute off, cycle, soft or OS reboot, and never automatically issue a second reset.
test_case.expected_result: The one reset request is accepted on the bound powered SUT; the prior boot instance ends, a new boot instance and console POST are observed, chassis power is On at the final checkpoint, and the OS plus approved services/storage/health recover within their timeouts. Expected reset events are present, no unexplained fault remains and the owner-approved final state is On/OS Ready.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact target, explicit approval, one reset, objective new-boot evidence, console POST, final canonical On and OS Ready/service/storage health. The preserved source word `off` is an internally contradictory defect and is not the executable expected result. Command acknowledgement, unchanged On status alone, a transient console disconnect, power Off, power cycle, graceful reboot or evidence from another variant cannot pass. Wrong target, unsupported/present-state rejection, no new boot, timeout, final Off, boot/storage/service failure or abnormal logs is FAIL; missing runtime bindings is NOT READY rather than Pending.
safety_gate: Require explicit approval immediately before the hard reset after rechecking exact target, initial On state, outage, workload drain, I/O quiescence and recovery readiness.
Preserve SEL, console, OS, storage and service evidence; do not clear logs or expose credentials.
Allow exactly one fixed reset operation and read-only monitoring; deny off, on, cycle, soft, policy writes and arbitrary commands.
Do not infer reset from On status alone and do not require or invent a transient Off state; use boot identity and console/POST evidence.
Stop on wrong target, unsupported response, lost BMC/console, no new boot, timeout, storage/filesystem/service/thermal/alarm anomaly or failed final On/OS Ready. Do not retry automatically.
Any incident-recovery power action requires separate human authorization outside the test sequence.
expected_evidence: Authoritative correction record, explicit approval, target identity, outage/risk acceptance and initial On/OS Ready/workload/health baseline
Pre-reset boot ID/uptime and console context; redacted one-time reset request/completion with pinned tool/Script versions
Timestamped reset transition, new boot ID/reset uptime, console reset and POST timeline
Final canonical chassis On, OS Ready, service/storage/filesystem/health and expected-event evidence
No-clear/no-substitution/no-retry audit, final On state and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: If reset or boot recovery fails, stop without another reset or alternate power command and retain all evidence. Use OOB console and the Project boot/storage recovery runbook under a separately authorized incident action; validate filesystem/storage/services and restore the approved On/OS Ready state before closure. Escalate any unresolved data-integrity or availability issue.

source_conflict.reason: Standard IPMI hard-reset semantics plus the same source sentence's booted-OS clause and normal-reset criterion resolve the isolated final `off` as a source defect. The review layer preserves that text but uses authoritative final On/new-boot acceptance.

blocked.reason: The core expected result is now defined by standard reset semantics and objective boot recovery. Exact target, outage, timers and recovery remain bounded Project prerequisites.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Exact SUT/BMC/console map; qualified reset path; outage/workload/I/O protections; reset/POST/OS/service timers; boot identity and event rules; final On state and incident recovery runbook.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; REVIEW-LAYER HYBRID CASE ONLY; NO IPMI, RESET, POWER, LOG, OS OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1
external_authorities.application: Section 28.3 defines hard reset as control value 3, distinct from Power Down and Power Cycle, and describes present-state handling.

external_authorities.title: ipmitool pinned power-control value mapping
external_authorities.application: Maps Reset separately from Down/Off, Up/On, Cycle and Soft, confirming that final Off is not the reset subcommand's semantic.

external_authorities.title: ipmitool pinned chassis implementation
external_authorities.application: Shows separate status and chassis-control paths, supporting post-command state parsing rather than equating acknowledgement with reset success.

project_authority: The Project owner supplies the exact target, abrupt-reset outage authorization, qualified implementation, workload/I/O controls, boot identity, POST/OS/service timeouts and incident recovery. It does not need to redefine the standard final reset state.
